# brig agent update

Move an agent's sandboxes to its current image, keeping their /sandbox

## Synopsis

```text
brig agent update [VM] NAME [SANDBOX...] [-w W] [--dry-run] [--yes] [--reset PATH]...
```

## Description

Move the sandboxes of an agent to the image that [`brig agent build`](brig-agent-build.md) last
built: find the template that agents/NAME/agent.yaml names, and recreate
every sandbox of that template whose image differs from the template's, as
[`brig sandbox recreate`](brig-sandbox-recreate.md) does. With SANDBOX arguments, only those move.
Sandboxes that [`brig sandbox run`](brig-sandbox-run.md) created are left alone.

It works through the sandboxes one at a time, stops at the first failure and
leaves the rest as they were, and prints a line for each sandbox. Each
sandbox keeps a snapshot from before the move.

Run --dry-run first: it checks each sandbox and prints what would happen,
such as programs that the move stops and policy rules that the sandbox has
and its policy file lacks. The sandboxes keep those rules, unless --policy
file gives each the policy file it came from.

Without VM, the one that [`brig use`](brig-use.md) selected is used. A first argument that
names a VM is the VM.

## Examples

```sh
brig agent build dev claude && brig agent update dev claude --dry-run
brig agent update dev claude
brig agent update dev pi kit-dev --reset .pi/agent/settings.json
```

## Options

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--dry-run` | print what would happen, and change nothing |
| `-o, --output format` | output format: table or json (default `table`) |
| `--policy string` | give the new sandbox this policy file, or with file, the sandbox's own (default: its current base policy) |
| `--reset stringArray` | leave PATH, relative to /sandbox, out of the restore, so that the new image sets it up (repeatable) |
| `-w, --workspace string` | the workspace of the gateway to work in (default: $BRIG\_WORKSPACE, else default) |
| `-y, --yes` | stop sandboxes without asking, also when a program runs in them |

The [global options](brig.md#options) of brig apply too.
